title: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element, all in constant time.
shortTitle: Min Stack — design with O(1) getMin (auxiliary min stack)

s1_definition.profdef: Min Stack is a data-structure design problem where you augment a normal stack so that the current minimum can be read in constant time. The standard technique keeps a second auxiliary stack that, at every level, stores the minimum of all elements present up to that point, so popping the main stack and the min stack together always keeps the minimum correct.
s1_definition.analogy: Rajesh is tracking the balance of his account after each transaction on a pile of slips. On top of each slip he also writes the lowest balance his account has ever reached up to that moment. When he removes the top slip, the "lowest ever" note on the new top slip is still correct, because it was recorded for that earlier state. So at any instant he can glance at the top slip and instantly know both the current balance and the lowest balance so far, without re-reading the whole pile.
s1_definition.oneliner: Keep a parallel min stack whose top always holds the minimum of everything currently in the main stack.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Min Stack is a data-structure design problem where you augment a normal stack so that the current minimum can be read in constant time. The standard technique keeps a second auxiliary stack that, at every level, stores the minimum of all elements present up to that point, so popping the main stack and the min stack together always keeps the minimum correct.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** Rajesh is tracking the balance of his account after each transaction on a pile of slips. On top of each slip he also writes the lowest balance his account has ever reached up to that moment. When he removes the top slip, the "lowest ever" note on the new top slip is still correct, because it was recorded for that earlier state. So at any instant he can glance at the top slip and instantly know both the current balance and the lowest balance so far, without re-reading the whole pile.

**One line to remember:** Keep a parallel min stack whose top always holds the minimum of everything currently in the main stack.

sections.s2_technical:
A normal stack gives you push, pop, and top in constant time, but finding the minimum would require scanning every element, which is linear. The trick is to trade a little extra memory for speed by maintaining a second stack that mirrors the main stack and records the running minimum.

When you push a value, you push it onto the main stack. For the min stack, you push the smaller of the new value and the current minimum. For example: `int min = minStack.isEmpty() ? value : Math.min(value, minStack.peek()); minStack.push(min);`. This way the top of the min stack is always the minimum of all values currently in the main stack.

When you pop, you pop both stacks together. For example: `mainStack.pop(); minStack.pop();`. Because the min stack was built in lockstep, removing the top of both keeps the invariant that the min stack top is the current minimum.

Reading the minimum is then just a peek. For example: `public int getMin() { return minStack.peek(); }`. This is constant time because it is a single array access, no scanning.

For banking money, you would not use `int`; you would use `BigDecimal` and `compareTo` instead of `Math.min`. For example: `BigDecimal min = minStack.isEmpty() ? value : (value.compareTo(minStack.peek()) < 0 ? value : minStack.peek());`. A senior nuance is the space optimization: instead of storing the minimum at every level, you can store only new minimums along with a count, or store the previous minimum before overwriting, which reduces memory when there are long runs of non-decreasing pushes. But the two-stack version is the clearest and is what interviewers usually expect first.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At National Bank of India, the risk desk watches Rajesh's intraday account balance as a sequence of states after each transaction. During the day they frequently need to answer "what is the lowest the balance has been so far?" to check whether an overdraft threshold was ever breached. Scanning the entire history each time is wasteful when it is asked thousands of times. This is exactly how Min Stack works — we record the running minimum alongside each pushed state so the lowest-so-far is available instantly.

Problem 2 — When a transaction is reversed, the system must pop the latest balance state and the "lowest so far" must automatically revert to what it was before that state. This is exactly the lockstep pop of the auxiliary min stack — removing the top of both stacks restores the earlier minimum correctly.

The mini-project builds a `BalanceMinStack` class that stores `BigDecimal` balances with `push`, `pop`, `top`, and `getMin`, a `RiskMonitorService` that uses it to track and log the lowest intraday balance, and a runnable demo that pushes and pops a sequence of balance states.

sections.s5_journey:
The input is a sequence of balances: 1000000, 850000, 920000, 600000, then a reversal, then 700000.

Step 1: Push 1000000. The min stack is empty, so the recorded minimum is 1000000. Main stack top is 1000000, min stack top is 1000000.

Step 2: Push 850000. The current min stack top is 1000000, and 850000 is smaller, so the recorded minimum becomes 850000. Main top is 850000, min top is 850000.

Step 3: Push 920000. The current minimum is 850000, and 920000 is larger, so the recorded minimum stays 850000. Main top is 920000, min top is 850000.

Step 4: Push 600000. 600000 is smaller than 850000, so the recorded minimum becomes 600000. Main top is 600000, min top is 600000.

Step 5: Reverse the last entry. Both stacks pop their top. The 600000 balance and its 600000 minimum are removed. The new min stack top is 850000, so the lowest-so-far correctly reverts to 850000.

Step 6: Push 700000. The current minimum is 850000, and 700000 is smaller, so the recorded minimum becomes 700000. Main top is 700000, min top is 700000.

```text
2026-10-26T16:20:00Z [INFO] National Bank of India — Intraday Balance Risk Monitor (SAV2001)
2026-10-26T16:20:00Z [INFO] Recorded balance 1000000 | lowest so far = 1000000
2026-10-26T16:20:00Z [INFO] Recorded balance 850000 | lowest so far = 850000
2026-10-26T16:20:00Z [INFO] Recorded balance 920000 | lowest so far = 850000
2026-10-26T16:20:00Z [INFO] Recorded balance 600000 | lowest so far = 600000
2026-10-26T16:20:00Z [INFO] Reversed 600000 | lowest so far = 850000
2026-10-26T16:20:00Z [INFO] Recorded balance 700000 | lowest so far = 700000
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```text
  push(1000000)    main:[1M]            min:[1M]
    │
  push(850000)     main:[1M,850k]       min:[1M,850k]
    │
  push(920000)     main:[..,920k]       min:[..,850k]  (min stays)
    │
  push(600000)     main:[..,600k]       min:[..,600k]  (new low)
    │
  pop() reversal   main:[..,920k]       min:[..,850k]  (min reverts)
    │
  push(700000)     main:[..,700k]       min:[..,700k]
    ▼
  getMin() → peek min stack top → O(1)
```
sections.s5d_lld:
```text
  ═══ LLD — Min Stack ═══

  ┌─ Design Patterns Used ───────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Auxiliary stack mirrors running minimum (invariant)      │
  │  BigDecimal.compareTo for money (never ==/<)              │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ SOLID ──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  S: BalanceMinStack stores; RiskMonitorService monitors   │
  │  O: swap min-tracking strategy without changing callers   │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │   BalanceMinStack                     │
  │  - mainStack: Deque<BigDecimal>       │ actual values
  │  - minStack:  Deque<BigDecimal>       │ running minimum
  │  + push(BigDecimal): void             │ O(1)
  │  + pop(): BigDecimal                   │ O(1)
  │  + top(): BigDecimal                   │ O(1)
  │  + getMin(): BigDecimal                │ O(1)
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  Invariant: minStack.peek() == min(all values in mainStack)

  Contract for push(v):
    Post: minStack.peek() = min(prevMin, v); size++ on both
  Contract for pop():
    Pre:  stack not empty (else IllegalStateException)
    Post: both stacks shrink by one; invariant preserved
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Min Stack is a design problem about trading a small amount of extra memory to make a query constant time. A normal stack already gives push, pop, and top in constant time, but finding the minimum would mean scanning everything. My solution keeps a second auxiliary stack that, at every level, records the minimum of all elements present up to that point. When I push, I push the value onto the main stack and push the smaller of the new value and the current minimum onto the min stack. When I pop, I pop both stacks together, which keeps the min stack top equal to the minimum of whatever remains.

The elegance is in the invariant: the top of the min stack is always the minimum of the current contents of the main stack, so reading the minimum is a single peek with no scanning. Popping in lockstep is what makes reversals correct, because the earlier minimum re-emerges naturally once the later state is removed.

For banking I use BigDecimal rather than primitives for the balances and compare with compareTo instead of equality or less-than operators, because money comparisons must respect scale and precision. If memory were tight, I would mention the optimization of storing only new minimums with counts, or storing the previous minimum before overwriting, but the clean two-stack version is the one I reach for first.

In my project at National Bank of India, I used this inside a risk monitor that tracks a customer's intraday balance as a stream of states. The desk constantly asks for the lowest balance so far to check overdraft thresholds, and the auxiliary min stack answers that instantly, while a reversed transaction simply pops both stacks and the lowest-so-far reverts to its earlier correct value without any recomputation.
